football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 1.7 points.
supporting: When TCU has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): TCU’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.6% of its dropbacks, and Baylor’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.7% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When TCU has the ball (the run game against the run defense): TCU’s offense averages 3.8 yards per carry, and Baylor’s defense allows 4.1 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).
When TCU has the ball (big plays on the ground): TCU’s offense turns 3.0% of its runs into explosive gains, and Baylor’s defense gives up explosive gains on 4.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When TCU has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): TCU’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 20.3% of its runs, and Baylor’s defense stops 22.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
contradicting: When Baylor has the ball (big plays on the ground): Baylor’s offense turns 5.5% of its runs into explosive gains, and TCU’s defense gives up explosive gains on 2.6% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put TCU’s pass defense No. 10 nationally and Baylor’s No. 83.
When Baylor has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Baylor’s offense averages 7.1 yards per pass attempt, and TCU’s defense allows 6.3 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.5).
When Baylor has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Baylor’s offense averages 4.7 yards per carry, and TCU’s defense allows 4.1 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

Jaden Craig has completed 107 of 156 passes (68.6%) for 1,393 yards, 8.9 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in five games for TCU, and has been sacked on 13 of 169 dropbacks.
